title: A circumbinary protoplanetary disk in a polar configuration
question: What are the orientation, size and structure of the circumbinary disc around HD 98800BaBb, and is it misaligned/polar and planet-forming?

data.sensitivity: rms 14 µJy/beam (Briggs); CO 0.8 mJy/beam per 0.73 km/s channel

what.value: BaBb orbit and combined mass 1.28 Msun

evidence.quote: We assume the CO orbits a single point mass with the combined mass of HD 98800BaBb of 1.28 M⊙ [17].

what.value: Radial velocities of AaAb and BaBb in early 1990s

evidence.quote: Ref [42] find that the systemic velocity of AaAb (12.75 km s−1) was more positive than BaBb (5.73 km s−1) in the early 1990s

what.value: Dust temperature of 160 K from multiwavelength photometry

evidence.quote: assuming a dust temperature of 160K derived from photometry over a range of wavelengths

recipe.method: Pipeline calibration, one phase self-cal, concatenate two EBs

recipe.goal: Model continuum and CO in visibility plane
recipe.method: Power-law ring line-of-sight integration model fit to visibilities; eccentric inner edge for continuum
assumptions: Distance 44.9 pc; CO orbits 1.28 Msun point mass

recipe.method: Optically thin dust mass from flux; CO mass assuming tau=1, Tex=70 K; H2/CO=1e4
MCMC orbit fit to WDS astrometry plus radial velocity constraints
assumptions: Mass of A 1.3±0.15 Msun prior; B 1.28 Msun

recipe.goal: N-body and SPH dynamics of the two disc orientations
recipe.method: Gas-free n-body with REBOUND whfast for 1 Myr; SPH with Phantom
Monte Carlo of 1e6 random orientations at 16 eccentricities, classify via constant of motion c vs e^2
assumptions: Uniform eccentricity 0-0.8, isotropic initial orientation, test-particle dynamics
